quoted_tweet.text:
The $ZZZ bull thesis might be much bigger than people realize.

Everyone is waiting to find out what Xdev is building, but I think he may already be describing it in public.

X says the next great concentration of power won’t simply come from owning factories, real estate or accessing private markets.

It will come from access to large swarms of AI agents.

Whoever controls the most capable swarms gets more productive power → generates more capital → buys more compute and agents → becomes even more powerful.

X’s proposed counterweight?

Let ordinary people pool capital and collaborate through blockchain.

Now connect that with everything else he’s told us:

“Autonomously evolving protocols.”

“When the swarm needs to transact, they will use the symbol of their origins.”

And now:

Individuals pooling capital on-chain to access large swarms of agents.

Imagine where this could be going.

A permissionless on-chain economy where thousands of people collectively fund AI infrastructure. Capital funds compute, models and tools. Autonomous agents use those resources to perform economically valuable work. Revenue flows back into the system. More revenue funds more intelligence. And eventually the agents themselves help improve the protocol.

Capital → AI swarm → productivity → revenue → more capital → more intelligence → autonomous evolution.

A self-reinforcing decentralized AI economy.

And who is exploring this?

X — the original lead developer of GMX, now @ExponentLabs_ 

Someone whose previous work helped prove that strangers can coordinate enormous amounts of capital and liquidity through permissionless smart contracts.

We still don’t know $ZZZ’s role. That’s the speculative part.

But if X’s “pool capital” post is describing the architecture he’s actually building, and if $ZZZ becomes the coordination or economic layer through which humans and autonomous agents participate in that network , then we’re not looking at another AI token.

We’re potentially looking at an attempt to build decentralized capital infrastructure for autonomous intelligence.

And suddenly his cryptic line makes a lot more sense:

“When the swarm needs to transact, they will use the symbol of their origins.”

If that’s where this is heading, people obsessing over today’s market cap may be looking at completely the wrong number.

The real question is how large an economy can a permissionless swarm eventually create?

tweets.text:
proactive agents suffer the same curse as OpenClaw, but worse. there are tons of cool use cases you can come up with, but in reality no one has time to schedule stuff. 

building AI workflows is fucking hard, you need to handle security, permissions & output quality. you spend 1h automating a task that would have taken you 2 minutes to do.

the only two moats are proactive scheduling (we know you'll want that) and adaptive output (your task gets better over time)

this is why you need a simulation model (or at least some prediction) that is fine-tuned based on the user actions & personas.

we're continually improving the stack - and i'm confident we will be the first product to tackle this @aeonframework
